text.text:
### Prerequisites

This game continues the previous game, in which we multiplied a number with tens and units by a number made up only of units (<htcite0>). Because every step here builds on that calculation, we suggest that you practice with that game before moving on, so that you can follow each step of the multiplication with ease.

text.text:
### A next step

Our understanding of multiplication has been evolving throughout the texts and applications published on History Tracers. So far, we have taken these steps:
- We learned that multiplication is the repeated addition of the same number (<htcite0>).
- We reinforced the idea of complementing a number: whenever it was necessary, we moved that value up to the next decimal place (<htcite1>).
- In the previous game, we moved from multiplying one single-digit number by another to multiplying a number with tens and units by a single-digit number (<htcite2>).

Our next step on this learning path is to multiply numbers with more than two digits (units, tens, hundreds, etc.) by a single-digit number. Now reflect on the following question:

text.text:
Reflection 1: Next step

With everything you have seen so far, how would you multiply a number with three, four, or even eight digits by a single-digit number?

The answer to this reflection is simple: we should follow exactly the same steps as before, only repeating each of them more times.

To make these new steps easier to picture, we will use once again the abacuses developed in China (Zhongguo, 中國), Japan (Nippon-koku or Nihon-koku, 日本国) and Russia.

### The Abacus (Multiplication)

Practice is what turns knowledge into skill (<htcite0>), so the abacus below guides you through a multiplication and explains, step by step, every stage of the calculation performed with this tool.

#### Levels

The game has 8 levels, one for each column of the abacus. Each level sets how many digits the first factor has:

- **Level 1**: 1-digit numbers (1 to 9)
- **Level 2**: 2-digit numbers (10 to 19)
- **Level 3**: 3-digit numbers (100 to 199)
- **Level 4**: 4-digit numbers (1,000 to 1,999)
- **Level 5**: 5-digit numbers (10,000 to 19,999)
- **Level 6**: 6-digit numbers (100,000 to 199,999)
- **Level 7**: 7-digit numbers (1,000,000 to 1,999,999)
- **Level 8**: 8-digit numbers (10,000,000 to 19,999,999)

When you feel ready, use the "⭐ Next level" button to move on to the next level.

#### Multiplier

Use the dropdown selector next to the level badge to choose the number you want to multiply by. Pick a specific number from 1 to 9, or choose "Randomly" to get a different multiplier in each exercise.

#### How to play

Between the bar with the "🎲 New exercise" and "⭐ Next level" buttons and the "➡️ Next step" button, you will see an instruction describing what to do at the current stage. As soon as you complete that stage correctly, a message congratulating you appears at the bottom of the abacus: "✅ Correct! Click 'Next step' to continue."

Keep following the steps until the calculation is complete; then you will receive the following message: "🎉🎉🎉 PERFECT! 🎉🎉🎉 Great job using the abacus!"

After you finish the 8th level, you will receive the following message: "🏅 Congratulations! You reached the last level! 🏅"

You can repeat as many exercises as you wish at the same level: simply click "🎲 New exercise" after finishing a calculation.

source.text: Costa, M., Cardoso, A. P., Lacerda, C., Lopes, A., & Gomes, C.
